current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Bug Report from Kevin

Body:
Hi, after the update today.  Some goals keep failing.  I had Claude analyze and this is what it concluded.

Regression: deny_unknown_fields in host-bound Skill completion contract rejects valid agent output

Offending commit: 25526f7a — "Bind Skill completion identity in the host instead of model output" (2026-09-12)
Severity: High — silently converts previously-tolerated agent completions into hard gate failures, wedging Goals that have otherwise passed their reviews.
Area: src/application/agent_io/contracts/skill_result.rs, src/application/events/completion.rs
Reported: 2026-09-14 · node bo2lnxipsapp01 · Refine 4.3.1

Summary

25526f7a moved routing identity (invocation_id/binding_id/role) host-side — a good change that removes a class of identity-echo failures. But as a side effect it introduced a new, stricter completion contract (SkillReport) carrying #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], replacing the tolerant SkillResult::decode path for all new (host_bound) completions. Any completion containing a field outside {outcome, summary, evidence, artifacts} — or any prose-wrapped output the envelope extractor reads as more than one JSON object — is now a hard Serialization error that fails the gate, where it was previously accepted (unknown fields were silently ignored).

The agent prompts were not updated to match this narrower shape, so there is now a contract↔prompt mismatch.

Root cause

Old contract (still in src/model/automation.rs:410) — no deny_unknown_fields, so serde ignored extra fields:

pub struct SkillResult {
    pub invocation_id: String,
    pub binding_id: String,
    pub role: String,
    pub outcome: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub summary: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub evidence: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub artifacts: Value,
}

New contract added by 25526f7a (skill_result.rs) and now used by decode_result(...) for host_bound receipts:

#[derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]          // ← new: any extra field is now fatal
pub(crate) struct SkillReport {
    pub outcome: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub summary: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub evidence: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub artifacts: Value,
}

completion.rs switched decode from SkillResult::decode(...) to decode_result(output, &id, &binding.id, &role, host_bound), routing all fresh completions through the strict SkillReport.

Note: the "reject 2 distinct JSON candidates" envelope logic itself is older (introduced ~2026-08-15, b1ba2b52/dfdebad4). 25526f7a didn't add that check — it narrowed the accepted object shape, which is what turned real-world agent output fatal.

Symptoms / evidence

Two failure signatures, both traced to this contract:

1. unknown field 'checklist', expected one of invocation_id, binding_id, role, outcome, summary, evidence, artifacts
   The plan skill instructs agents to produce "stable checklist IDs," so the model emits a top-level checklist field. Pre-25526f7a: ignored. Post: deny_unknown_fields → hard reject at the plan gate.
2. contains 2 distinct JSON candidates; exactly one is required
   The configured agent (claude-opus-4-8) wraps its answer in prose. Captured raw result events from failed quality/governance invocations begin with prose, not JSON:
   - governance: "Governance review complete. **Outcome: success — no violations found.** …"
   - plan: "I've fully analyzed the round. Here is my plan-step result. …"
     (result_starts_with_json = false in every failed case.) The envelope extractor then finds the prose-embedded JSON plus the object and refuses to disambiguate.

The agents are completing the actual reviews correctly — one governance run even self-diagnosed the quality fault as an output_contract_fault and recommended re-running. Only the output envelope is rejected.

Because it's probabilistic (1175+ Goals have completed successfully), it presents as intermittent "flaky harness" faults; affected Goals exhaust the repair loop and hard-fail.

Impact

- Goals that pass constitution/quality/governance can still fail at the gate purely on envelope shape, and land in failed with category plan / workflow / governance_integration.
- Repair loop (structured-output-repair) does not reliably recover it — the model keeps re-emitting prose/extra fields, and max_repairs is not operator-configurable.
- Retrying a failed gate can churn an already-passed stage back to output_contract_fault (observed on Goal 00000T130287HH5HPK5QJ8C014: quality had passed, re-run dragged it back to a contract fault).

Observed affected Goals (node bo2lnxipsapp01):
- 00000T130287HH5HPK5QJ8C014 (high) — repeated output_contract_fault at quality/governance, 2 distinct JSON candidates.
- 00000T137KN16JMJFY73J8C018 (low) — unknown field 'checklist' at plan, then 2 distinct JSON candidates at implement.

Recommended fix (upstream)

Pick one; first is lowest-risk:

1. Make SkillReport decode tolerant of unknown fields — drop #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], or strip unknown top-level fields host-side before decoding. This restores the pre-25526f7a tolerance while keeping the host-bound identity improvement. (Extra fields like checklist should be ignored or lifted into artifacts, not fatal.)
2. Harden envelope extraction so a single well-formed contract object embedded in prose is accepted rather than rejected as "2 distinct JSON candidates" — or strip non-JSON preamble/trailer before parsing.
3. Reconcile the prompts with the contract — the plan skill still asks for checklist IDs; either add checklist to the accepted contract or instruct agents to nest plan/checklist structure under artifacts.

A combination of (1) + (3) addresses both failure signatures at the source.


[cid:insurity-small2_60d9d841-975e-4326-81a1-42eb773307d1.jpg]

Buddy Williams

VP & Forward Deployed Engineer

T +1-860-616-2578

default-governance.name: Governance
default-governance.prompt:
## Governance

Verify that the implementation meets the user-defined Goal, fits the system architecture, and serves the project's purpose.

### Outcome

A clear assessment of whether the implementation satisfies all three. Begin with the verdict, then briefly explain how the work meets the Goal, fits the architecture, and supports the project's purpose, using concrete evidence from the implementation and Quality results. For each gap, describe what falls short, why it matters, and the recommended correction. Separate necessary corrections from optional improvements.

### Guardrails

- Read the context that helps explain the user's Goal, the system architecture, and the project's purpose.
- Compare the implementation with the user's desired outcome as well as the plan. Completing the plan and passing tests alone do not establish that the Goal is met.
- Look for clear responsibilities, shared behavior implemented in one place, and interfaces that remain easy to use and maintain.
- Judge design choices by how they serve the project. Allow sound approaches that differ from personal preference.
- Group related issues by their underlying cause so the next step can address them together.

{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

default-quality.name: Quality
default-quality.prompt:
## Quality

Test the implementation. Create and groom tests to cover the behavior described in the plan.

### Outcome

Meaningful tests cover the changed behavior and pass. Provide a brief report of the behavior tested, tests added or updated, commands run and their results, and any remaining failures or gaps. Include runtime or browser test results where useful. These results support Governance's verification of the work.

### Guardrails

- Test observable behavior, including relevant failure cases and effects on existing functionality. Tests should catch defects rather than mirror the implementation.
- Keep useful tests, update tests for changed behavior, and remove obsolete or meaningless tests.
- Investigate failures, correct problems in the implementation or tests, and rerun affected tests.
- Choose tests suited to the change. Expand coverage when failures or affected behavior call for it.

{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

default-plan.name: Plan
default-plan.prompt:
## Plan

Develop a plan to achieve the Goal's desired outcome. If the goal outcome is underspecified or is missing details add only just enough detail so that AI agents do not thrash or become confused.

### Outcome

A clear implementation plan that explains the approach and breaks the work into ordered tasks. Begin with a short description of the desired behavior and proposed solution. Use a numbered checklist, such as `Task #1 - What changes and why`. Include dependencies and important design decisions where they help implementation.

### Guardrails

- Read the context that helps explain the Goal and how the existing system works.
- Look for the underlying cause. Consider whether a missing or misused concept explains the problem, and improve that concept rather than adding fixes for individual symptoms.
- Give each task enough detail to guide implementation while leaving room for reasonable implementation choices.
- Keep the plan focused on the desired outcome. Prefer straightforward changes that fit the existing architecture.

{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

default-plan.summary:
Accept Skill completions with harmless extra fields while preserving host-bound identity, verdict validation, and rejection of ambiguous output. Clarify prompts so optional planning and review details belong inside the completion contract.

1. [ ] Task #1 - Add regression fixtures. Cover top-level checklist and other extra fields, identity-free reports, matching legacy identities, partial or mismatched identities, invalid outcomes, and malformed known fields. Cover direct, fenced, enveloped, and prose-wrapped JSON, plus two distinct completion objects. The current extractor already accepts prose around one object; prose alone does not establish an extraction bug.

2. [ ] Task #2 - Separate content tolerance from identity validation in src/application/agent_io/contracts/skill_result.rs. Extract the bounded completion value once, then explicitly select the identity path. For host-bound receipts without identity fields, decode tolerant provider content and attach host identity. If any identity field is present, require all three fields and exact matches. Legacy receipts must continue requiring matching identity. Ignore unrelated top-level fields at this application boundary, preserve known context fields, and retain required-field, type, and outcome validation. Keep the persisted model strict. Do not merely remove deny_unknown_fields: that would silently accept mismatched identities through the current report-first fallback. Preserve useful decoding diagnostics instead of replacing report errors with legacy-schema errors.

3. [ ] Task #3 - Resolve only demonstrated envelope defects. Use Task #1 fixtures to verify existing extraction and deduplication. Preserve rejection of genuinely distinct JSON candidates and conflicting envelope fields; do not select the last successful-looking verdict. If a fixture demonstrates that one logical response is counted twice, fix that extraction case while retaining payload, nesting, and envelope limits. The supplied report lacks full raw outputs, so the exact two-candidate failure remains unconfirmed.

4. [ ] Task #4 - Align initial and repair prompts. Update supervised-skill.md and skill-repair.md to request exactly one final JSON object, with prose in summary and structured plans/checklists under artifacts. Keep supporting context optional and the contract generated from SkillReport. Inspect shipped workflow Skill instructions for conflicting output directions; current prompts already omit identity and do not require a checklist.

5. [ ] Task #5 - Verify completion and replay behavior. Extend lifecycle tests to show tolerant reports retain their verdict and context, bind the correct identity, and replay retained receipts without another provider launch. Confirm invalid identities, malformed decisions, and ambiguous results still fail. Run cargo test, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and git diff --check. Keep repair budgets, workflow retry policy, and automatic recovery of previously failed Goals outside this change.

From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Bug Report from Kevin

Body:
Hi, after the update today.  Some goals keep failing.  I had Claude analyze and this is what it concluded.

Regression: deny_unknown_fields in host-bound Skill completion contract rejects valid agent output

Offending commit: 25526f7a — "Bind Skill completion identity in the host instead of model output" (2026-09-12)
Severity: High — silently converts previously-tolerated agent completions into hard gate failures, wedging Goals that have otherwise passed their reviews.
Area: src/application/agent_io/contracts/skill_result.rs, src/application/events/completion.rs
Reported: 2026-09-14 · node bo2lnxipsapp01 · Refine 4.3.1

Summary

25526f7a moved routing identity (invocation_id/binding_id/role) host-side — a good change that removes a class of identity-echo failures. But as a side effect it introduced a new, stricter completion contract (SkillReport) carrying #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], replacing the tolerant SkillResult::decode path for all new (host_bound) completions. Any completion containing a field outside {outcome, summary, evidence, artifacts} — or any prose-wrapped output the envelope extractor reads as more than one JSON object — is now a hard Serialization error that fails the gate, where it was previously accepted (unknown fields were silently ignored).

The agent prompts were not updated to match this narrower shape, so there is now a contract↔prompt mismatch.

Root cause

Old contract (still in src/model/automation.rs:410) — no deny_unknown_fields, so serde ignored extra fields:

pub struct SkillResult {
    pub invocation_id: String,
    pub binding_id: String,
    pub role: String,
    pub outcome: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub summary: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub evidence: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub artifacts: Value,
}

New contract added by 25526f7a (skill_result.rs) and now used by decode_result(...) for host_bound receipts:

#[derive(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]          // ← new: any extra field is now fatal
pub(crate) struct SkillReport {
    pub outcome: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub summary: String,
    #[serde(default)] pub evidence: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)] pub artifacts: Value,
}

completion.rs switched decode from SkillResult::decode(...) to decode_result(output, &id, &binding.id, &role, host_bound), routing all fresh completions through the strict SkillReport.

Note: the "reject 2 distinct JSON candidates" envelope logic itself is older (introduced ~2026-08-15, b1ba2b52/dfdebad4). 25526f7a didn't add that check — it narrowed the accepted object shape, which is what turned real-world agent output fatal.

Symptoms / evidence

Two failure signatures, both traced to this contract:

1. unknown field 'checklist', expected one of invocation_id, binding_id, role, outcome, summary, evidence, artifacts
   The plan skill instructs agents to produce "stable checklist IDs," so the model emits a top-level checklist field. Pre-25526f7a: ignored. Post: deny_unknown_fields → hard reject at the plan gate.
2. contains 2 distinct JSON candidates; exactly one is required
   The configured agent (claude-opus-4-8) wraps its answer in prose. Captured raw result events from failed quality/governance invocations begin with prose, not JSON:
   - governance: "Governance review complete. **Outcome: success — no violations found.** …"
   - plan: "I've fully analyzed the round. Here is my plan-step result. …"
     (result_starts_with_json = false in every failed case.) The envelope extractor then finds the prose-embedded JSON plus the object and refuses to disambiguate.

The agents are completing the actual reviews correctly — one governance run even self-diagnosed the quality fault as an output_contract_fault and recommended re-running. Only the output envelope is rejected.

Because it's probabilistic (1175+ Goals have completed successfully), it presents as intermittent "flaky harness" faults; affected Goals exhaust the repair loop and hard-fail.

Impact

- Goals that pass constitution/quality/governance can still fail at the gate purely on envelope shape, and land in failed with category plan / workflow / governance_integration.
- Repair loop (structured-output-repair) does not reliably recover it — the model keeps re-emitting prose/extra fields, and max_repairs is not operator-configurable.
- Retrying a failed gate can churn an already-passed stage back to output_contract_fault (observed on Goal 00000T130287HH5HPK5QJ8C014: quality had passed, re-run dragged it back to a contract fault).

Observed affected Goals (node bo2lnxipsapp01):
- 00000T130287HH5HPK5QJ8C014 (high) — repeated output_contract_fault at quality/governance, 2 distinct JSON candidates.
- 00000T137KN16JMJFY73J8C018 (low) — unknown field 'checklist' at plan, then 2 distinct JSON candidates at implement.

Recommended fix (upstream)

Pick one; first is lowest-risk:

1. Make SkillReport decode tolerant of unknown fields — drop #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], or strip unknown top-level fields host-side before decoding. This restores the pre-25526f7a tolerance while keeping the host-bound identity improvement. (Extra fields like checklist should be ignored or lifted into artifacts, not fatal.)
2. Harden envelope extraction so a single well-formed contract object embedded in prose is accepted rather than rejected as "2 distinct JSON candidates" — or strip non-JSON preamble/trailer before parsing.
3. Reconcile the prompts with the contract — the plan skill still asks for checklist IDs; either add checklist to the accepted contract or instruct agents to nest plan/checklist structure under artifacts.

A combination of (1) + (3) addresses both failure signatures at the source.

Buddy Williams

VP & Forward Deployed Engineer

T +1-860-616-2578
